summary: This is a well-documented, preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment that measures the marginal effect of inserting a deterministic network verifier plus one automated repair call into an LLM intent→configuration pipeline under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Execution and archiving appear thorough and reproducible. However, the manuscript currently reads more like an evidence manifest than a conventional conference paper; a small but important set of clarifications and presentation changes are required before finalisation.
critical_issues: Manuscript presentation is metadata/provenance-heavy and reads like an artifact report rather than standard scholarly prose; this undermines readability and proper scientific positioning (must be rewritten to standard conference-paper narrative while preserving artifact references).

Statistical reporting and interpretation need clearer exposition: the reported exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 is surprising to many readers and the manuscript must state precisely how the exact test is computed (statistical definition or formula, relation to the two-sided exact binomial on discordant pairs), why p=1.00 arises for the observed n=1 discordant pair, and the practical implication for inference under extreme ceiling effects.

The manuscript omits a brief, explicit description of the single discordant episode in the Results (pair identifier and short summary of validator violation code and repair applied). Without that concise pointer in the paper body, readers cannot readily verify the claim that the verifier+repair corrected a real baseline failure (the artifact store contains the record, but the paper must point to it unambiguously).
required_revisions: Rewrite the main manuscript (Introduction, Related Work, Methods, Results, Discussion) into conventional literature-grounded conference prose: move detailed provenance, step-by-step artifact-retrieval instructions, long hash lists, and per-file lookup guidance into a short reproducibility subsection or a compact paragraph referencing the archived evidence bundle (all of which are available). Preserve all archival identifiers but compress their in-text presentation to increase information density and narrative flow.

Add a brief, explicit description of the single discordant pair in the Results: include the archived pair_id (from execution/raw_results.jsonl), the validator violation code(s) and severity, and a one-sentence summary of the repair prompt/response that produced the guarded pass. This information is available in the supplied artifacts and must appear in the paper to substantiate the claimed corrected instance.

Provide precise methodological/statistical detail in Methods and Results about the exact McNemar implementation: state the test formula used (exact binomial on discordant pairs or alternative exact convention), the two-sided p-value computation rule applied by the archived analysis executor, and why p=1.00 occurs for the observed discordant counts. Also report the one-sided exact p-value (or otherwise justify two-sided choice) and include the paired-bootstrap procedure details (resampling unit, strata preservation, B=10000, seed), all of which are present in the analysis artifacts.

Explicitly state that secondary per-violation-class analyses were not informative or were not performed due to near-zero violations, and that the planned power assumptions (preregistration) did not hold because baseline error prevalence was far lower than assumed; discuss consequences for interpretability (ceiling effect) and whether any preregistered sensitivity analyses were invoked. This can be resolved using the archived execution and analysis artifacts.

Clarify and justify the preregistered 'generation_semantics = shared_initial_candidate' choice in Methods (why it isolates verifier+repair conditional on identical proposals), and explicitly state this experimental scope and limitation in the Abstract and Introduction so readers correctly interpret what effect was measured versus other possible verifier-driven generation strategies.
optional_revisions: Add one compact table (<=1/2 page) summarising preregistered vs observed quantities that materially diverged from assumptions (expected baseline error rate, planned model-call budget, actual model_calls_used, repairs invoked) to help readers quickly see why the study encountered a ceiling effect. All values are available in the evidence bundle.

Briefly discuss (in Limitations) how different generation semantics (e.g., verifier-guided regeneration, larger repair budgets, iterative repair) could materially change observed verifier benefits and point to which archived artifacts would support such follow-on analyses.

Consider adding a short schematic figure illustrating the shared_initial_candidate vs independent-generation semantics to help readers unfamiliar with the distinction; this is optional but would improve accessibility.
